notes.meaning: This passage opens the family record of Adam, focusing on the godly line leading down to Noah. God created humanity in His own holy likeness, making both male and female with equal honor. He blessed them and named them "man," joining husband and wife together as one.

differ.view: Many Reformed Christians believe biblical family lists often leave out generations and were never meant to calculate the exact age of the earth.

notes.meaning: Adam was created in the likeness of God, but after turning away in sin, he fathered a son in his own fallen likeness. Seth inherited Adam's mortal, sinful nature rather than the perfect moral image his father had at first. Even so, God chose Seth's family line to carry on true worship and the holy promise of a rescuer.

Adam lived for many centuries after Seth's birth and had many more sons and daughters. His long life gave his descendants the chance to hear directly from him about creation, the fall, and God's promises. Yet after 930 years Adam died, showing that God's warning that sin brings death always comes true.

Seth fathered Enosh and lived for 912 years while raising a large family. God gave these early fathers long lives so the world would be filled with people and true faith would be passed down clearly. In the end, Seth also died, proving that even the most godly fathers could not escape physical death.

Enosh became the father of Kenan and lived over nine centuries before his life ended. The steady repetition of the phrase "and he died" shows that sin's curse of death rules over all mankind. We are reminded that no matter how long someone lives, everyone must eventually face death.

Kenan's life followed the same pattern of having children, living many years, and finally dying. Scripture lists these names carefully to show that God deeply values those who love and worship Him. Each generation carried the hope of God's promise forward despite the reality of bodily death.

Mahalalel lived 895 years in the fear of God before passing away. God kept the memory of these early believers alive while evil was growing rapidly across the world. His long lifespan allowed him to guide and teach his children in the truth over many generations.

Jared lived 962 years, making him the second oldest person in the Bible. He faithfully raised his children and passed the knowledge of God down to his son Enoch. Even with such an extraordinary lifespan, his earthly story still closed with the words, "and he died."

Enoch was 65 years old when he became the father of Methuselah. Becoming a parent likely deepened his devotion and his desire to follow the Lord with his whole heart. Methuselah's name also served as a warning, pointing to the judgment of the flood that would come when he died.

Enoch lived in close friendship and daily agreement with God for 300 years while raising his family. Walking with God means making God's will our guide and seeking to please Him in everything we do. This shows that true godliness fits naturally into the ordinary duties and joys of family life.

differ.view: Some Methodists believe Enoch's walk shows that believers can receive grace to live completely free from sin and please God in all things.
Reformed Christians believe Enoch walked in genuine, steady faith, but no believer in this life is entirely free from sin.

notes.meaning: Enoch lived 365 years, which was short compared to the other men, but his life was completely devoted to God. Instead of dying, he was taken straight into heaven, body and soul, because God was pleased with him. God gave this miraculous event to comfort His people with the sure hope of a better life after this world.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Many ancient church teachers believed Enoch and Elijah are the two witnesses who will return to preach before the end of the world.

notes.meaning: Methuselah lived 969 years, the longest lifespan of anyone mentioned in Scripture. His long life was a wonderful display of God's patience, giving people time to turn from their evil ways before the flood. Yet even the man who lived the longest could not escape physical death in the end.

Lamech named his son Noah, a name connected with rest, hoping for relief from the hard labor caused by the curse on the earth. He spoke with the spirit of prophecy, looking ahead to how God would bring comfort and preservation through Noah. This longing also points to Christ, who gives real rest to weary souls under the weight of sin.

Lamech lived for 777 years, raising other children before his earthly life came to a close. He passed away just a few years before the great flood, being spared from the terrible judgment that fell on the world. His life ended in the quiet hope that God would soon bring mercy to His people.

Noah was 500 years old when he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Shem is listed first because the covenant promise and the family line of Jesus Christ would run through him, even though Japheth was likely older. God chose this single household to start the human race anew after the flood waters receded.
